views.label: Closed universe

legend: the equator of space at one moment

stops: In the flat universe every moment is flat, and its equator is a plane.
caption: The equator ($\theta = \pi/2$) of the closed universe from $\eta = -3$ to $3$, each moment a sphere of radius $a = \ell - A\cos\eta$, smallest at the bounce, $\eta = 0$.

views.label: Open universe

legend: the equator of space at one moment, out to $\chi = 1$

views.settings: $\ell = 1$ and $A = 3/2$, with lengths measured by $dX^2 + dY^2 - dZ^2$.
stops: At every $\chi > 0$ the circles grow faster than the distance out to them, so no surface of revolution in flat space carries the moment; Minkowski space carries it.
caption: The equator ($\theta = \pi/2$) of the open universe, each moment a hyperboloid in Minkowski space, smallest at the bounce, $\eta = 0$.
